feedback.Dismiss: ACCURATE TRIAGE: Correctly dismissed authorized off-hours database replication. Checking the destination IP (10.0.9.15) showed it was the company's internal Disaster Recovery vault, and the process was the scheduled cron job 'replicate_dr_snapshots.sh'. Good false-positive discipline!
feedback.Escalate: MINOR PENALTY: Escalated routine scheduled database replication to Tier 2. The ticket number CHG-AUTO-DR-SYNC and internal destination IP confirmed this was expected operations.
feedback.Block IP: OPERATIONAL DISRUPTION: Blocked the internal Disaster Recovery storage vault 10.0.9.15! Nightly backups failed to replicate across the enterprise.
feedback.Isolate Host: CRITICAL PRODUCTION OUTAGE: You isolated the primary production database server SRV-DB-PROD01! All customer transaction processing was knocked offline.

educational_rationale.topic: Off-Hours Data Transfers vs Scheduled DR Backups (False-Positive Discipline)
educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Security+ SY0-701 (Section 3.1 Business Continuity & DR Operations, Section 4.2 Triage Verification) & Network+ (Section 4.2 Network Policies & Asset Categorization)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: Large data transfers at 03:00 AM are not inherently malicious. A mature analyst examines the destination: Is it an untrusted public cloud storage bucket (e.g. wasabisys.com), or an internal RFC 1918 Disaster Recovery subnet (10.0.9.15)? They examine the process: Is it an unapproved third-party tool like rclone executing from a user Temp directory, or the corporate PostgreSQL cron script running under service account 'postgres'? Verifying the corporate Change Management system (CHG ticket) separates benign operational maintenance from active insider exfiltration.
